quote: Curry roux is wheat-flour based and the signature toppings are breaded/fried cutlets and croquettes, so wheat is pervasive throughout the kitchen.
found: Gnavi page carries the cutlet/roux half only: 「『金沢カレー』とは…濃厚でどろっとした黒いルーが特徴のカレー！代表的なメニューがロースカツカレー。」 and 「お客様にアツアツ揚げたてをお召し上がりいただけるよう、ご注文を頂いてから心をこめて作っております。」 It never says the roux is wheat-flour based and never mentions a croquette. The croquette half is on the operator's own menu page: 「クリームコロッケカレー ホワイトソースから作る玉ねぎたっぷりの自家製クリームコロッケ。」 plus ロースカツ/チキンカツ/エビフライ.

Neither page states the curry roux itself contains wheat flour — soften that to 'thick dark roux, wheat flour not declared' or cite an allergen source.

quote: Menu is centered on pork cutlet, sausage, hamburg steak and a meat-stock roux; no plant-based items are documented.
found: The cited page documents a vegetable curry in its own こだわり block: 「【季節限定メニュー】金沢の伝統野菜「加賀野菜」を使ったオリジナルカレーが味わえます。秋から春にかけては、加賀れんこんと五郎島金時の天ぷらを盛り付けた野菜好きのためのカレー。野菜が好きな方や健康志向の方におすすめのメニューです。」 The operator's menu page adds 野菜玉子カレー. The page also never says the roux is meat-stock based.
note: 'No plant-based items are documented' is contradicted by the cited page itself, which advertises a seasonal Kaga-vegetable curry (renkon + Gorojima sweet-potato tempura). vegan_status 'no' still stands — the same dark roux and wheat tempura batter are shared — but reword to 'a seasonal vegetable curry exists, but on the shared meat-stock-style roux'. Separately: gorp and the official site both give hours as 11:00–20:00 (L.O. 19:30) 年中無休, while the record carries 11:00-21:00 (L.O. 20:30).

quote: The chestnut paste itself uses only Noto aged roasted chestnuts with no added sugar, so the chestnut element is naturally simple.
found: 「オーダーを受けて絞る、完全無糖の能登焼栗ペースト。」 and 「栗という素材100％のおいしさ」
note: Verbatim. Article is from 2022-06-18; the shop is still trading (official site currently advertises new 茶房席予約 seat booking via airrsv.net).

why: The shop publishes per-product allergen declarations and does tick 小麦 where it applies (薄墨 pound cake 「アレルギー表記：卵、乳、小麦」; 二藍 and 菓子詰め合わせ 「乳、小麦、卵」), yet declares 乳 only for 朱華 and 橡 — both 「和栗をねりこんだ葛ねりと…和栗ペーストの新しい形のモンブラン」, i.e. kuzu-starch rather than flour — and 「アレルギー表記：なし」 for 茶鼠 (えがらまんじゅう of 和栗餡 in a 自家製粉したもち米 dough). A blanket 'Not gluten-free / Not safe for celiacs' misreads a shop that labels wheat honestly and sells items it declares wheat-free. 'ask' is the right tier: the in-café flagship 榛摺 really does contain スフレ・スポンジ, the kitchen is shared, and 支子 declares 乳 only while its description mentions スフレスポンジ — an inconsistency a celiac must resolve at the counter.

The record says 'No vegan dessert option is documented', but the shop's own page for 茶鼠 describes 「和栗のえがら 煉 neriは、契約農家で丁寧に育てられた和栗を餡にし、自家製粉したもち米の生地で包み上げた特別な一品」 with 「■アレルギー表記：なし」 — chestnut an in a self-milled glutinous-rice dough, no egg, no dairy declared. That is a documented plausibly-vegan item; 'ask' rather than 'no'.

method: 1 plain fetch + linked PDF, text via PyMuPDF (pdftotext returned mojibake)
note: Backwards on the point that matters. The shop does not offer to advise: it states the kitchen does not separate utensils, dishes or fryer oil, uses wheat flour, dairy and egg throughout, guarantees no separation, and puts the decision on the diner after consulting a doctor. Rewrite as: 'publishes a per-item 29-allergen chart (Japanese only) but explicitly disclaims any separation of equipment or fryer oil and puts the judgement on the diner.' The transparency is a real positive; the reassurance is not.
